research_question: Does geodesic farthest-point-sample initialization spread the swarm over the vessel graph while satisfying joint Euclidean and geodesic separation constraints, with a recorded bounded relaxation ladder?
main_variable: initialization_mode='separated' (spawn rule only). No reward, observation, physics or action-semantics change.

implementation.sampling: geodesic FPS over station candidates (excludes distal cap); random proximal seed station; joint constraints

constraints.min_euclidean: 8 robot radii (dimensionless relative to the device)

implementation.relaxation_ladder: R0 strict; R1 both minimums halved; R2 geodesic only; R3 unconstrained FPS (always terminates). Level + achieved minima reported per reset; no unbounded retry loop.
implementation.scope_statement: The Euclidean minimum is a GEOMETRIC PROXY for disjoint local control regions. There is no magnetic-field model in this repository and this experiment does not claim to simulate one.

invariants.legacy_default: initialization_mode='legacy' reproduces historical trunk placement bit-identically

validation.pytest: tests/test_separated_initialization.py: constraints hold at level 0 across anatomical scenarios; ladder bounded under infeasible constraints (no deadlock); spread exceeds legacy cluster; legacy unchanged; vector env mode
validation.measured: 14 anatomical scenarios x 8 episodes, 5 robots, default constraints: 112/112 resets at relaxation level 0; min pairwise Euclidean 0.0715 (required 0.0176); min geodesic fraction 0.196 (required 0.12)
validation.smoke: scripts/run_scaling_smokes.sh separated_init: 448 transitions, PPO update finite

performance_claim: none: whether separated spawns improve success is a training question requiring new 1M-transition runs
